findings.title: §3.5o sub-point #3 (Free disk space composite step) NOT applied — 14 heavy-cargo workflows still lack the step despite R6-FP-D's L19-r1-MAJ-1 sweep claiming closure
findings.evidence: R6-FP-D commit 36988d1a ('ci(r6-fp-d): close L17-MIN-1 + L19-MAJ-1 + L19-MIN-1/2/3/4 — flip ts-public-api to required-failing + §3.5o env-var sweep across 24 workflows...') explicitly SCOPED to env vars only: the commit body's `§3.5o disk-OOM env vars (CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 + CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only) applied workspace-wide to 24 Rust-compiling workflows that previously lacked them.` The commit makes NO mention of adding `Free disk space` composite steps. However the L19-r1-MAJ-1 disposition explicitly required all 3 sub-points: 'FIX-NOW — single R6-FP commit applies §3.5o env vars (the 2 env vars + a `Free disk space` step where missing) to every Rust-compile-doing workflow. Atomic-shape: add a top-level `env:` block with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0` + `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only` to each workflow currently lacking it, AND add the `- uses: ./.github/actions/free-disk-space` step (with `if: runner.os == "Linux"`) immediately after checkout on every Linux job leg.' The §3.5o codification at .addl/dispatch-conventions.md (point #3) is unambiguous: 'every Rust-compile-doing workflow' — it frees ~25-30 GB of unused tooling. Ground-truth audit at HEAD 3c80546f: 14 heavy-cargo workflows MISSING the Free disk space step: admin-shell-e2e.yml (cargo build --release benten-admin-shell --features tauri); bench.yml (cargo bench --workspace --no-run); bundle-size.yml (wasm32 release builds); cite-drift.yml (cargo build --release); cross-browser-determinism.yml (wasm32 release builds with --profile release-wasm); cross-process-graph.yml (cargo nextest run with many features); determinism.yml (wasm32-wasip1 release builds); fuzz.yml (cargo test); host-error-wire-safety.yml (cargo nextest run); msrv.yml (cargo build --workspace — the workflow that explicitly documents disk-pressure in its own L70-77 comments; the env vars now in place but Free-disk-space half still missing); supply-chain.yml (cargo build --locked --workspace — heavy workspace build); ts-public-api.yml (napi build via pnpm + cargo); wasm-browser.yml (cargo check wasm32 + release build); wasm-runtime.yml (cargo check wasm32-wasip1 + cargo test). All 14 fail point #3 of the §3.5o discipline. The composite action exists at `.github/actions/free-disk-space/` (verified) so the fix is purely additive. The 8 workflows that DO have the step: ci.yml (3 steps), coverage.yml (2), multi-arch-cargo-check.yml (2), packages-engine-vitest.yml (2), devserver-vitest.yml (3), phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml (8), napi-vitest.yml (2, added at R6-FP-D MIN-3 close), wasm-conformance.yml (2). The pattern is: workflows that historically OOM'd or were touched by prior fix-passes have it; workflows that haven't yet OOM'd (but compile cargo) don't — exactly the failure-mode the §3.5o codification was meant to break.
findings.ground_truth_verify: Reproducer: `for f in .github/workflows/*.yml; do has_cargo=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*[\$]?run:.*cargo |cargo [a-z]' $f | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' | wc -l); has_fds=$(grep -c 'Free disk space\|free-disk\|jlumbroso' $f); if [ "$has_cargo" -gt 0 ] && [ "$has_fds" -eq 0 ]; then echo "MISSING: $(basename $f)"; fi; done` returns the 14 file list above at HEAD 3c80546f. Cross-check the §3.5o codification: `grep -A 1 'Free disk space.*Linux runners only' .addl/dispatch-conventions.md` returns the rule text. Cross-check the R1 disposition: the L19-r1-MAJ-1 disposition string in the R6 R1 L19 JSON explicitly names both env vars + Free disk space step as part of the FIX-NOW shape.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — single orchestrator-direct R6-FP-R2 commit that adds `- uses: ./.github/actions/free-disk-space` step (or the equivalent `- uses: jlumbroso/free-disk-space@...` pattern matching ci.yml's shape) immediately after the `actions/checkout` step on every Linux job leg in the 14 listed workflows. Per §3.5o codification 'Apply at workflow-env scope so every matrix leg inherits — macOS legs are no-ops there (~40 GB free) so no special cases needed' — add the step unconditionally where the leg is Linux-only; gate with `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` on matrix-os legs that include macOS (admin-shell-e2e.yml + multi-arch-cargo-check.yml + ci.yml already have it correctly gated; cold-install.yml has matrix.os too). Closure pin: after the R6-FP-R2 commit lands, re-run the reproducer above and confirm 0 MISSING lines. The §3.6j sweep-completeness-self-verify rule explicitly requires running the validation against the wave's own outputs BEFORE claiming COMPLETE — apply that discipline here.

findings.title: CARGO_INCREMENTAL value format inconsistent across workflows (unquoted `0` in 3 workflows vs quoted `"0"` in 24 workflows)
findings.evidence: The 3 workflows that originally carried §3.5o env vars (ci.yml + coverage.yml + wasm-conformance.yml — all pre-existing before the R6-FP-D sweep) use unquoted YAML integer `CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0`. The 24 workflows that got the env vars added via R6-FP-D commit 36988d1a + fix-up #9's mint use quoted YAML string `CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"`. Both forms parse correctly (YAML parses one as int + the other as str; GitHub Actions converts both to env-var-string `0` at runner-bind time). The functional behavior is identical but the style inconsistency is mild. Python yaml.safe_load round-trip verified: ci.yml gets int 0 + msrv.yml gets str '0'.
findings.ground_truth_verify: Reproducer: `python3 -c "import yaml; [print(f, type(yaml.safe_load(open(f)).get('env',{}).get('CARGO_INCREMENTAL', None)).__name__) for f in ['.github/workflows/ci.yml','.github/workflows/msrv.yml','.github/workflows/wasm-conformance.yml','.github/workflows/coverage.yml']]"` shows mixed types. Functional check: `grep -nE 'CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "?0' .github/workflows/*.yml` enumerates both forms.
findings.disposition: OBSERVE — no action at R6 R2. If a future R6 round 3+ sees additional drift-class candidates, fold this normalization into the same fix-pass (~3-line edit; pick `"0"` as the canonical form since it matches the dominant 24-vs-3 split). Not gating.

lens_reflection.what_the_lens_is_uniquely_positioned_to_: Process-side hygiene drift in workflow files + the spec ↔ live branch-protection diff (which no other R6 lens surfaces — code-side lenses look at code, threat-model lenses look at adversary frames, doc-coupling lenses look at prose). The §3.5o sub-point #3 (Free disk space step) coverage gap + the wider apply-runbook deferral gap are pure infrastructure-class surfaces that no other lens has angle on. The §3.6j sweep-completeness-self-verify discipline applies recursively: R6 R1 L19 sweep itself FAILED §3.6j on its own L19-r1-MAJ-1 closure (claimed sweep COMPLETE but only sub-points #1+#2 applied) — exactly the failure-mode §3.6j was codified to break.
lens_reflection.what_this_lens_did_not_check: Per-workflow CORRECTNESS of the cargo invocations themselves (whether the right tests run with the right features) beyond the -p+features reachability audit — broader test-coverage scoping is L13 territory. Runtime/environment failures inside workflows (e.g., admin-shell-e2e's tauri-driver port-binding failure surfaced at L19-R2-OBS-2) — those are L13 or a platform-runtime lens. Per-workflow security posture of dependencies (cargo-deny rules themselves) — those are L2 adversarial or supply-chain-specific lens territory.
lens_reflection.cross_check_pair_notes: L19 has no formal cross-check pair in the R6-LENS-CATALOG.md §'Cross-check pairs' table. Its outputs feed the §3.6j sweep-completeness-self-verify discipline by exercising the published catalog against live state — a meta-check the catalog itself recommends. R6 R2 cross-confirms L19 against L17 (frozen-interface) + L18 (breaking-change-ledger) for the API drift gates — all three lenses see consistent state on cargo-public-api.yml + ts-public-api.yml as required-failing.
